title: rustup, Cargo, and a first project

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “rustup, Cargo, and a first project” to a real program or device. The key principle is: Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects. In a project, follow this guidance: Obtain the installer from rust-lang.org and install native prerequisites only for the target you need.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
EXAMPLE CODE

spans.code:
rustc --version
cargo --version
cargo new hello-rust
cd hello-rust
cargo run

spans.text: EXPECTED RESULT
Cargo creates, compiles, runs, and tests a project; version/build summaries vary by toolchain.
CORE EXPLANATION

Install Rust with the official rustup installer. It manages rustc, Cargo, and components such as rustfmt; Cargo handles project creation, builds, tests, and dependencies.

Origin and dates: Graydon Hoare began Rust as a personal project in 2006; Mozilla sponsored the work from 2009, and Rust 1.0 shipped on May 15, 2015. Its purpose was to combine low-level control with memory safety and safe concurrency, addressing risks such as use-after-free and data races. Rust is now used for command-line tools, servers, browser components, and embedded firmware; it is relevant to systems, backend, embedded, compiler, and tooling careers. If you enjoy making ownership and resource use explicit while building fast, reliable software, Rust is worth exploring.

On Windows, download the official rustup-init.exe from the Rust site; an MSVC target may also need the C++ build tools from Visual Studio Build Tools. On macOS, use the official rustup installer and install Xcode Command Line Tools if native builds require them. On Linux, run the official rustup installer; crates needing a C library may also require your distribution's compiler and development packages. Reopen the terminal and check rustc and Cargo versions. Select the target triple explicitly for production builds.

rustup installs and updates toolchain components and targets. rustc checks and compiles source code; Cargo manages the manifest, builds, tests, and dependency resolution. `cargo new` creates a binary or library crate, `cargo check` performs a fast type check, and `cargo run` builds and executes. Release builds enable optimizations and differ from development builds.
IMPORTANT LINE BREAKDOWN

Key line: `cargo new hello-rust`
What it does: Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects.
Why it is used: Obtain the installer from rust-lang.org and install native prerequisites only for the target you need.
If omitted or changed: rustup manages toolchains and targets; Cargo manages project builds, dependencies, and tests.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Check PATH changes on managed computers; MSVC and GNU targets can require different linkers and native dependencies.
